en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Monkey.

7. The Question on the Three Qualities of the Jewel-Treasure “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘three qualities of the jewel-treasure are to be adopted,’ which are those three qualities to be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the jewel-treasure is absolutely pure;”
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the spiritual life, must be one whose livelihood is entirely pure.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the jewel-treasure that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the jewel-treasure is not mixed with anything else.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the spiritual life, should not associate with evil people or evil companions.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the jewel-treasure that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the jewel-treasure is set in precious settings.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the spiritual life, should dwell together with those who possess the most excellent and noble birth;

he should dwell together with the jewel-like ascetics who are stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, and arahants— those established in the fruits of practice, those still in training, and those possessing the three knowledges,
the six super-knowledges, and the sixfold higher powers.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the jewel-treasure that should be adopted.
And this was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God beyond Gods, in the Sutta Nipāta:
“Pure ones dwell together with the pure;”
“Live together with mindfulness;
then, being harmonious and prudent,
you shall make an end of suffering.”
The seventh question: The Jewel-Treasure Limb.
